findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the material_components / material_fingerprint consistency invariant is mechanically enforced (a single shared basis-builder both call, or a test that asserts the composite of the per-component inputs equals material_fingerprint for the same ctx), given pass1.py cannot be edited.
evidence: Plan: 'material_components(ctx) returns {name: hash16} ... hashing exactly the same per-key values material_fingerprint already feeds into the composite (so the two can never disagree)'

pass1.py:761-776 builds `basis` inline (including _normalize_checkbox_state(ctx.description) and sorted child ids) then does json.dumps(basis, sort_keys=True) — a single composite hash, not per-key sub-hashes
Scope: 'pass1.py is at 776 of the 800-line cap ... pass1.py is not touched' — so the shared basis-construction cannot be centralized in pass1 without touching it
findings.finding: The claim that material_components and material_fingerprint 'can never disagree' is asserted but not mechanically guaranteed: per-component hashing is a structurally different computation from the single composite JSON-blob hash, and the basis-construction they must share (basis dict assembly, checkbox normalization of `description`, and children enumeration) currently lives inline in pass1.material_fingerprint, which the plan explicitly forbids touching.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (material_diff.material_components); Scope note 'pass1.py is not touched'
scenarios: A future edit to material_fingerprint's basis (e.g. a new key, or a change to checkbox normalization) is not mirrored in material_diff, so the composite says stale-material but explain_material_change names no differing component (or a wrong one)
material_components normalizes `description` differently from pass1 (or forgets to), producing a spurious `description` diff on a tick-only edit and breaking the 330c checkbox-safety test
findings.suggested_fix: Have material_diff.material_components build the basis by calling a small extracted helper that material_fingerprint also uses, OR add a test that constructs a ctx, computes both material_fingerprint(ctx) and a composite re-hash of material_components' pre-hash inputs, and asserts they match — so any future basis drift fails CI rather than silently disagreeing.
